title: Traffic Harbor Playbook for Staged Experiments (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
- Create a compact, operational playbook for running incremental traffic experiments across Redwood Console that treats traffic slices like a harbor: controlled mooring points, tide-aware scaling, and emergency egress lanes.
- Provide a pragmatic checklist and signal matrix product + SRE + data + solutions teams can use to run low-risk progressive rollouts for LLM features (model swaps, rerankers, latency-tiering, fallback routing).

Why 'Traffic Harbor' metaphor:
- Harbor = place to stage and hold traffic safely before releasing to open sea (full prod). Motivates concepts: mooring (small steady slices), breakwater (fallback capacity), tide (diurnal/seasonal load), weather-room (stakeholders/obs during exposure).
- Helps non-engineering stakeholders reason about exposure and safety without heavy ops jargon.

High-level goals:
- Fast experiments with clear safety bounds.
- Predictable unit economics (token cost impact must be visible before widening exposure).
- Clear rollback and fallback that do not require urgent infra changes.

Core concepts & primitives:
- Mooring slice: stable cohort (e.g., 0.1% of traffic) pinned to an experiment config and observation window.
- Tidal window: time-of-day and traffic-volume constraints; run slices when tide is favorable (low conc.) for early canaries.
- Breakwater policy: pre-configured fallback capacity (model variant or lower-cost route) to absorb traffic spikes or quality regressions.
- Mooring anchor: commitment signal (visibility in Console + Slack) that means the experiment is "anchored" and not subject to immediate auto-scaling expansion.
- Weather-room: a temporary channel + dashboard for the exposure, including on-call, product PM, data owner, and dev owning the change.

Signal taxonomy (priority order):
1) Safety signals (stop immediately): catastrophic errors, P95 latency > 5x baseline, rate of confidence-rejected responses > 3x baseline, user-affecting NPS regression in top customer slices.
2) Health signals (pause/reduce): sustained 2x latency P50–P90 for 15m, token cost per request > 1.5x expected, error budget burn > 30%/hour.
3) Quality signals (investigate): semantic drift on eval prompts > threshold, increase in manual moderation flags, conversion metric delta exceeding guardrail.
4) Economic signals (throttle): long tail token cost growth without quality improvement.

Traffic partitioning heuristics:
- Start with deterministic moorings (by user_id hash) to prevent cohort contamination during A/B measurement.
- Prefer orthogonalization by device or client version for early safety slices (reduces downstream correlated effects).
- Reserve a floating "storm-slice" (0.01–0.05%) that can be diverted instantly into breakwater to test emergency mode.

Activation cadence (example):
- Prep (Day 0): experiment definition + hypothesis + primary metric + owner + linked tickets. Create weather-room.
- Anchor (Day 1): deploy config to staging; smoke test with synthetic traffic; validate observability hooks (traces, tracing keys, token counts).
- Moor 1 (Day 2): open 0.05% deterministic traffic for 1–2 hours during low tide; SRE monitors; product observes user-facing metrics.
- Observe (Day 2–3): run automated checks at 5, 15, 60 minute intervals; create preliminary report.
- Expand (Day 3–5): if green, widen to 0.5% then 1% separated by 12–24h windows; ensure cost gating prevents expansion if token/unit cost exceeds threshold.
- Ramp to cohort (Day 6+): expand to target segments in waves; maintain weather-room for final gate.

Experiment readiness checklist (pre-deploy):
- Clear hypothesis + metric owner.
- Defined stop / pause conditions in the Console rollout config.
- Observability: dashboard with P50/P90/P95 latency, token counts per route, model-specific output quality checks, request traces.
- Linked artifacts: runbook, JIRA ticket, eval set and baseline outputs, release notes draft.
- Fallback routes available and tested (mock traffic into fallback).
- Billing guardrails set (monthly/experiment budgets, per-token alerts).
- Stakeholder assignments and on-call rotation set for weather-room.

Runbook quick actions (when something trips):
- Safety alarm: flip traffic to breakwater for affected slices; mute feature flag; notify exec/CS if customers affected.
- If latency spike: divert a percentage of traffic to a lower-latency model and throttle batching.
- If quality drift: enable automated A/B scoring to isolate cohort responses; pause expansion.
- Post-incident: capture artifacts, attach to Jira incident, schedule postmortem within 3 business days.

Measurement & statistics:
- Use deterministic assignment to preserve ATE. Prefer Buckets with stable hashing and warmup periods excluded from analysis.
- Capture both online signals (latency, error) and offline evals (prompt sets, reranker precision@k).
- Minimum detectable effect and power calc required for any expansion beyond 1% traffic.
- Use drop-in evaluation traffic (synthetic user journeys) to validate semantics unchanged.

Simulation and rehearsal:
- Run a lightweight simulator before real traffic: replay production traces at 1x and 5x load into the experiment config.
- Conduct a "harbor drill" quarterly to test the entire play: anchor, moor, expand, trigger breakwater, rollback.
- Log results to a shared doc: what failed, time to recovery, and manual steps executed.

Operational ergonomics & Console features requested:
- Single-click "anchor" that locks expansion for 24h with reason field.
- Fast-press breakwater toggle that reroutes selected mooring slices to fallback instant.
- Per-experiment budget slider with enforced stop when hit.
- Built-in weather-room link generator that seeds dashboard, Slack channel, and incident template.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to balance deterministic assignment vs. user-level fairness for features that target only a subset of customers (enterprise customers vs. consumers).
- When to prefer time-based expansion windows vs. signal-driven expansion (we currently bias toward time windows for predictability).
- How much automation for automatic rollback (risk of noisy signals causing flip-flop).

Next steps (action items):
- [Asha] Prototype anchor UI in Console (Rough mock by 2025-12-15).
- [Miguel] Add "storm-slice" routing into serving runtime simulation (Sim PR ENG-4217, due 2025-12-05).
- [Riley] Draft weather-room incident template and Slack bot auto-invite (due 2025-12-01).
- [Eva] Run first harbor drill with internal reranker feature on 2025-12-08; produce drill report.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider "ebb mode": automatic conservative throttling during platform-wide high-latency events to prevent cascading failures.
- Could expose mooring analytics as a small billing insight card: "cost per moor" to help PMs reason about run economics.
